source.title: Optimizer Choice and Calibration for QARiB on Arabic-Script Social Media Offensive Language Detection

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer-related held-out performance in a new setting: QARiB fine-tuning for Arabic offensive-language detection on two datasets.
record.gate_note: Reports test-set comparisons among Adam, AdamW, and SGD. Threshold-tuning and temperature-scaling findings are not extracted as optimizer generalization results; cited prior-work findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance after fine-tuning QARiB with Adam, AdamW, and momentum SGD on two Arabic classification benchmarks. This tests V4 in a new setting, although its weight-decay tuning extends beyond V4's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: tuned Adam and AdamW perform similarly and outperform SGD under the tested budget, with SGD showing greater seed variability, especially in AUC-PROFF. The authors also conclude that temperature scaling produces modest, dataset-dependent calibration changes.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes QARiB, an Arabic encoder Transformer, on two imbalanced offensive-language datasets with a controlled learning-rate, weight-decay, and warmup grid; best settings are selected by validation macro-F1. It reports held-out test metrics, not train–test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and optimizer choice; AdamW and Adam are indistinguishable on OffensEval20 where selected weight decay is zero, while they differ slightly on MPOLD.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer-dependent calibration and modest, dataset-dependent temperature-scaling effects are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects probability calibration in QARiB fine-tuning; post-hoc temperature scaling has dataset-dependent effects.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says code/configuration files will be released after acceptance in an anonymized repository.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2nd Workshop on NLP for Languages Using Arabic Script (AbjadNLP 2026), Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Only one encoder model family and two Arabic benchmarks are tested. Test metrics are means and standard deviations over three seeds; the authors note limited statistical power. No training performance is reported, so the train–test gap itself cannot be assessed.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible optimizer held-out performance rows were left out. Calibration, threshold-tuning, and qualitative probability examples were not cataloged as V4 optimizer generalization results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.

Training-performance comparisons; tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules; a controlled narrow-versus-broad tuning comparison; recovery specifically attributable to decoupled weight decay or switching optimizers; word-level language modeling.
Batch-size comparisons and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Additional held-out discrimination results corroborate the optimizer ranking. MPOLD accuracy: AdamW 0.9028 ± 0.0025, Adam 0.9117 ± 0.0060, SGD 0.6983 ± 0.0312; ROC AUC: 0.9369 ± 0.0041, 0.9352 ± 0.0085, 0.7408 ± 0.0381, respectively. OffensEval20 accuracy: AdamW/Adam 0.9555 ± 0.0052, SGD 0.9112 ± 0.0076; ROC AUC: AdamW/Adam 0.9780 ± 0.0024, SGD 0.9428 ± 0.0069.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numeric values match Table 2. Missing training scores do not prevent assessing the held-out optimizer ranking, but prevent distinguishing optimization failure from a generalization-gap difference. The claimed equal tuning budget needs qualification: Adam/AdamW vary weight decay and warmup, whereas SGD fixes weight decay; the stated preliminary learning-rate grid also excludes the ultimately selected SGD rate of 1e-4. Three seeds and short, early-stopped training constrain interpretation.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Train performance, language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight-decay recovery, and whether adaptive methods do better on word-level language models.
Batch-size effects and adaptive large-batch training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

relationships.condition: QARiB fine-tuning on MPOLD with validation-selected learning rate, weight decay, and warmup, at most five epochs
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show Adam/AdamW outperforming momentum SGD: macro-F1 0.8356/0.8174 versus 0.6091 and AUC-PROFF 0.7891/0.7812 versus 0.4252. This identifies a setting with the opposite ranking; V4 already allows tuning-dependent reversals.
relationships.display_finding: Reported macro-F1 and AUC-PROFF advantages for Adam and AdamW over momentum SGD remain unverified.

relationships.condition: QARiB fine-tuning on OffensEval20 with validation-selected configurations, at most five epochs
relationships.reason: R7–R12 show Adam and zero-decay AdamW outperforming momentum SGD: macro-F1 0.9305 versus 0.8670 and AUC-PROFF 0.9397 versus 0.7971. This qualifies the scope of an adaptive-method disadvantage without contradicting V4's allowance for reversals.
relationships.display_finding: Reported macro-F1 and AUC-PROFF advantages for Adam and zero-decay AdamW over momentum SGD remain unverified.
